subject: Environment
sub_topic: National Biodiversity Authority — composition and functions

concepts.name: NBA: Statutory Basis and Parent Legislation
key_dimensions: Established under Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (Section 8) — not a constitutional body
Implementing body for Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), 1992 ratified by India
Distinction from bodies under Environment Protection Act, 1986 vs. BD Act, 2002
Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) — NBA as focal point for implementation

concepts.name: NBA Headquarters and Jurisdictional Character
key_dimensions: Headquartered in Chennai — trap question vs. MoEFCC in New Delhi
Operates at national level; contrast with State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) at state level and BMCs at local level
Three-tier structure: NBA → SBB → Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)
Jurisdiction extends to matters involving foreign nationals/entities and Indian companies with foreign equity

concepts.name: Composition of NBA: Chairperson and Members
key_dimensions: Chairperson: eminent person with knowledge/experience in conservation — appointed by Central Government
Ex-officio members: representatives from multiple ministries (Agriculture, Ocean Development, AYUSH, etc.) — exact count a frequent trap
Non-official members: experts from scheduled tribes, industry, fisheries, and academia
Total composition: Chairperson + ex-officio members + non-official members — distinctions matter for MCQs

concepts.name: NBA as a Statutory Autonomous Body: Legal Personality
key_dimensions: Corporate body with perpetual succession and a common seal
Can sue and be sued — quasi-judicial character
Distinction from advisory bodies: NBA has regulatory and adjudicatory powers
Funded by Central Government grants + fees from approvals — financial autonomy angle

concepts.name: Prior Approval (Access and Benefit Sharing) Function of NBA
key_dimensions: Mandatory prior approval for: foreign nationals/entities, NRIs, and Indian companies with foreign participation accessing biological resources
Section 3 of BD Act — no person shall obtain biological resources without prior approval of NBA
Trap: Indian individuals and local communities do NOT need NBA approval — they notify SBBs
Benefit Sharing Agreement as a condition of approval — link to Nagoya Protocol obligations

concepts.name: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Oversight by NBA
key_dimensions: Prior approval of NBA required before applying for any IPR (patent, etc.) based on biological resources from India — Section 6
Trap: applies to Indian nationals too when seeking IPR — unlike Section 3 which exempts Indian individuals for access
NBA can oppose grant of IPR in India or abroad if biological resources obtained without approval
Link to biopiracy prevention: Neem, Turmeric, Basmati case studies as context

concepts.name: Regulation of Transfer of Research Results and Third-Party Transfer
key_dimensions: NBA approval needed for transferring results of research relating to biological resources to foreign nationals (Section 4)
Distinction from Section 3 (access) and Section 6 (IPR) — three separate approval triggers
Collaborative research between Indian and foreign institutions must route through NBA
UPSC trap: confusing Section 3, 4, and 6 obligations as a single requirement

concepts.name: NBA's Role in Biodiversity Heritage Sites
key_dimensions: Central Government notifies Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS) on recommendation of State Government — NBA advises
Section 37 of BD Act — distinction: State Government recommends, Central Government notifies
NBA's role is advisory/recommendatory here, not the notifying authority — a key trap
Examples: Nallur Tamarind Grove (Karnataka), Kath Kuni Village (HP) — linkage to PBR and BMC data

concepts.name: NBA and People's Biodiversity Registers (PBR)
key_dimensions: PBRs are prepared by BMCs but NBA sets guidelines and provides oversight framework
PBR documents local biological resources, knowledge, and practices — not a legal entitlement document per se
Trap: PBRs are maintained by BMCs, not by NBA or SBBs directly
Link to Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) — complementary but separate instrument under CSIR

concepts.name: Benefit Sharing Mechanisms and the National Biodiversity Fund
key_dimensions: Section 41-44: Benefit claimants include conservers, creators, and holders of biological resources/knowledge
National Biodiversity Fund (NBF) receives fees and royalties collected by NBA
Fund used for conservation, protection, and development of areas from where resources are accessed
Distinction: NBA collects and routes funds; actual conservation work may involve local bodies

concepts.name: NBA's Adjudicatory and Appellate Powers
key_dimensions: NBA can compound offences under Section 24 — quasi-judicial function
Appeals against NBA orders go to High Court — NOT to NGT (a common trap)
NBA can file complaints to judicial magistrates for offences under the BD Act
Distinction: NBA adjudicates biodiversity disputes; NGT handles environmental cases under specific scheduled Acts

concepts.name: Exemptions from NBA Prior Approval — the 'Local Use' Carve-out
key_dimensions: Exemptions under Section 7: local communities, vaids, hakims, and Indian nationals for personal/local use do not need NBA approval
Growers and cultivators of biodiversity and practitioners of traditional medicine are exempt from NBA but must notify SBBs
Trap: exemption is from NBA approval only — SBB notification may still apply
AYUSH practitioners: partial exemption — codified vs. non-codified medicine distinction matters

concepts.name: State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) vs. NBA: Functional Demarcation
key_dimensions: SBBs regulate access by Indian nationals (non-exempt) — NBA regulates foreign/corporate access
SBBs set guidelines for use of biological resources within state for commercial purposes
NBA can issue directions to SBBs — hierarchical relationship but SBBs are state-level statutory bodies
Overlap trap: NBA and SBBs both involved in ABS but at different scales and for different actors

concepts.name: NBA's Powers to Restrict Prohibited Items and Notify Threatened Species
key_dimensions: Central Government can notify items in consultation with NBA as 'Normally Traded Commodities' — exempted from Section 3 approval
NBA advises on listing threatened species — link to Wildlife Protection Act's Schedule overlap
NBA can declare certain biological resources as 'prohibited' for export/access for conservation reasons
Distinction: CITES implementation is via DGFT/WPA, not NBA — UPSC overlap trap

concepts.name: NBA and International Obligations: Nagoya Protocol Implementation
key_dimensions: India ratified Nagoya Protocol in 2012 — NBA designated as national focal point (competent national authority)
ABS Clearing House Mechanism: NBA responsible for publishing permits and information on ABSCH portal
Internationally Recognised Certificate of Compliance (IRCC) — issued by NBA for legitimate access
Trap: Nagoya Protocol is a supplementary agreement to CBD, not a standalone treaty — NBA links both

concepts.name: NBA's Advisory and Policy Formulation Functions
key_dimensions: Advises Central Government on biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, and equitable sharing matters
Can recommend conservation of specific biological resources and impose restrictions
Advises on selection of biological resources for research and bioprospecting
Distinction: advisory role to Central Government vs. regulatory/approval role for applicants — dual character

concepts.name: Offences, Penalties, and Enforcement Under BD Act via NBA
key_dimensions: Section 55: penalties up to ₹10 lakh for contraventions — imprisonment possible for repeat offences
Companies liable: every person in charge of company at time of offence is liable (Section 56)
NBA can suo motu initiate action against biopiracy or unauthorized access — proactive enforcement
Trap: penalties under BD Act vs. Wildlife Protection Act vs. Forest Act — different regimes, different bodies enforce

concepts.name: NBA, Traditional Knowledge, and Indigenous Community Rights
key_dimensions: Section 36(4): National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) must mainstream traditional knowledge
NBA must ensure equitable benefit sharing with knowledge holders including tribal communities
Linkage with Forest Rights Act, 2006 — overlap in protecting forest-dwelling community knowledge
Trap: NBA does not grant land rights or IPR to communities — it only ensures benefit sharing from commercial use

concepts.name: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) — NBA's Role
key_dimensions: Section 36 mandates Central Government to develop NBSAP with NBA as key technical body
India's NBSAP revised in 2014 to align with Aichi Biodiversity Targets (CBD COP10, Nagoya)
NBA coordinates with state-level biodiversity strategies — vertical integration role
Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework (Kunming-Montreal, COP15, 2022): 30x30 target — NBA's updated mandate

concepts.name: NBA vs. Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) and TRAFFIC: Institutional Overlaps
key_dimensions: WCCB under MHA deals with wildlife crime enforcement — NBA deals with access and benefit sharing
TRAFFIC (Trade Records Analysis of Flora and Fauna) is an NGO network — not a statutory body, unlike NBA
NBA does not enforce CITES — DGFT issues CITES permits; NBA's mandate is BD Act-specific
UPSC trap: confusing NBA's biopiracy prevention role with WCCB's anti-poaching/trafficking mandate
